source:
Reports request matchers in an authorizeHttpRequests / authorizeRequests chain that are unreachable because an earlier, more general matcher already covers them.

Spring Security evaluates matchers in declaration order and the first matching rule wins, so a specific rule placed after a more general one that also matches it is silently ignored. More specific matchers must come first.

Incorrect (the marked rules are ignored):


  http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers("/", "/home").permitAll()
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/home").hasRole("USER")        // covered by the earlier "/home"
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/**").hasRole("USER")
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/test2").hasRole("ADMIN") // covered by the earlier "/test1/**"
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
  );

Correct (most specific first):


  http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/home").hasRole("USER")
    .requestMatchers("/", "/home").permitAll()
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/test2").hasRole("ADMIN")
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/**").hasRole("USER")
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
  );
target:
Meldet Request-Matcher in einer authorizeHttpRequests- / authorizeRequests-Kette, die nicht erreichbar sind, weil ein früherer, allgemeinerer Matcher sie bereits abdeckt.

Spring Security wertet Matcher in der Deklarationsreihenfolge aus, und die erste passende Regel gewinnt. Eine spezifische Regel, die nach einer allgemeineren steht, die ebenfalls passt, wird daher stillschweigend ignoriert. Spezifischere Matcher müssen zuerst stehen.

Falsch (die markierten Regeln werden ignoriert):


  http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers("/", "/home").permitAll()
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/home").hasRole("USER")        // durch das frühere "/home" abgedeckt
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/**").hasRole("USER")
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/test2").hasRole("ADMIN") // durch das frühere "/test1/**" abgedeckt
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
  );

Richtig (spezifischste zuerst):


  http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/home").hasRole("USER")
    .requestMatchers("/", "/home").permitAll()
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/test2").hasRole("ADMIN")
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/**").hasRole("USER")
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
  );
